Chapter 21 Reinforced and prestressed concrete sections

A concrete section does not respond linearly: concrete in tension cracks, concrete in compression becomes plastic, steel yields, and prestress imposes on its tendons an elongation that the concrete does not share. The elastic properties of chapter 20 are therefore no longer sufficient; for each action effect (N,My​,Mz​), the strain plane of the section that balances it with the laws of the materials must be found. This is the problem dealt with in this chapter, at serviceability (stresses, cracking, curvature) and at the ultimate limit state (resisting moment, interaction diagrams, required reinforcement), according to EN 1992-1-1 and, where the code provides them, EN 1992-2 and the German national annex. It also covers prestress losses at section level, the shear, torsion and punching shear formulae, slab reinforcement by Wood-Armer, and the checks of composite beams (EN 1994-1-1) and steel members (EN 1993-1-1 and 1-5) that keta provides. Prestress at the scale of the structure (profile, friction, equivalent loads) is in chapter 8, creep and shrinkage in chapter 9, the material nonlinearity of the bars of a framework in chapter 18, fire resistance in chapter 23.

keta computes values here: neutral axes, stresses, crack widths, resisting moments, steel areas. It pronounces no verdict: it does not itself compare a utilisation ratio with 1, and it applies no partial factors other than those the user gives it.

21.1 Assumptions#

  • plane sections remain plane (Navier-Bernoulli): the strain is a plane ε(y,z)=ε0​+κy​z−κz​y, positive in tension;
  • bonded reinforcing bars and bonded tendons have the strain of the concrete at their level, increased by their initial strain; an unbonded tendon keeps the force of its initial elongation;
  • concrete is described by a uniaxial law (parabola-rectangle, bilinear relation, Sargin law, straight line), without tensile strength unless a softening law is explicitly given; steels by a symmetric uniaxial law;
  • the laws are read as they are given: design values for the ultimate limit state, mean or characteristic values without partial factor for serviceability;
  • the section is a set of polygonal outlines with voids; steels are points; the concrete they displace is deducted on request;
  • shear force and torsion take no part in the equilibrium of the section: they are handled by the separate formulae of EN 1992-1-1 § 6.2 to 6.4;
  • creep enters the serviceability states through the effective modulus Ecm​/(1+φ), and the losses through the age-adjusted effective modulus method; the ultimate law is not stretched by creep.

21.2 Design laws of the materials#

21.2.1 Concrete: parabola-rectangle and simplified relations#

The basic law is the parabola-rectangle of EN 1992-1-1 § 3.1.7(1), expression (3.17), written in shortening εc​>0:

σc​=fcd​[1−(1−εc2​εc​​)n]  (0≤εc​≤εc2​),σc​=fcd​  (εc2​≤εc​≤εcu2​)(21.1)

The parameters are those of table 3.1: n=2, εc2​=2 ‰ and εcu2​=3.5 ‰ up to C50/60, and beyond

n=1.4+23.4(10090−fck​​)4,εc2​=2.0+0.085(fck​−50)0.53 ‰,εcu2​=2.6+35(10090−fck​​)4 ‰(21.2)

(fck​ in MPa). The exponent and the two strains may also be given freely. The exponent 1 gives the bilinear relation of § 3.1.7(2), a straight line up to fcd​ at εc3​ then a plateau up to εcu3​; keta derives εc3​=1.75 ‰ (beyond C50/60, 1.75+0.55(fck​−50)/40 ‰) and εcu3​=εcu2​. For rectangular or T sections treated in closed form, the rectangular stress block of § 3.1.7(3) is available: a stress ηfcd​ over the depth λx, with

λ=0.8−400fck​−50​,η=1−200fck​−50​(fck​>50 MPa; 0.8 and 1 below)(21.3)

At serviceability, cracked concrete follows a straight line of slope Ecm​ (or the effective modulus) in compression and carries nothing in tension.

21.2.2 Concrete: Sargin law and tension softening#

For nonlinear analysis, keta offers the law of EN 1992-1-1 § 3.1.5, expression (3.14), in compression only up to εcu1​:

fcm​σc​​=1+(k−2)ηkη−η2​,η=εc1​εc​​,k=1.05fcm​Ecm​εc1​​(21.4)

Its parameters come from table 3.1 when only fck​ is given: fcm​=fck​+8 MPa, Ecm​=22(fcm​/10)0.3 GPa, εc1​=0.7fcm0.31​≤2.8 ‰, εcu1​=3.5 ‰ up to C50/60 and 2.8+27((98−fcm​)/100)4 ‰ beyond. For C30/37, keta finds Ecm​=32.84 GPa, εc1​=2.16 ‰ and k=1.96, and its stresses reproduce (21.4) to within rounding. When used for a resistance, this law must be given with design values, as § 5.8.6(3) requires. A variant of the parabola-rectangle carries a softening tension branch: a straight line up to ft​ at εcr​=ft​/Et​, then a linear decrease to zero at

εtu​=εcr​+ft​lc​2Gf​​(21.5)

so that the energy dissipated per unit crack area is the fracture energy Gf​, whatever the band width lc​ (crack band method). A conventional law for class T3 ultra-high performance fibre-reinforced concretes (NF P18-710) is also available for fibre sections.

21.2.3 Reinforcing steel and structural steel#

Reinforcing steel follows the design diagram of figure 3.8 of EN 1992-1-1, symmetric in compression: a straight line of slope Es​ up to εyd​=fyd​/Es​, then an inclined branch up to the limit strain εud​,

σs​=fyd​+(ftd​−fyd​)εud​−εyd​εs​−εyd​​(εyd​≤εs​≤εud​)(21.6)

The resistance engine describes it by (fyd​,Es​,ftd​,εud​), by default B500 with ftd​=525/1.15 MPa at εud​=25 ‰; it may be extended by a plateau at ftd​ up to a higher limit strain. A horizontal branch is obtained with ftd​=fyd​. In fibre sections, the same figure is described by the class of the steel, k=(ft​/fy​)k​ and εuk​: the branch passes through (εuk​,kfyd​) and stops at εud​≤εuk​. Structural steel follows a symmetric bilinear law with a plateau at fy​, with an optional limit strain.

21.2.4 Prestressing steel#

Prestressing steel follows the design diagram of figure 3.10 (§ 3.3.6(7)): a straight line of slope Ep​ (195 GPa for strands, 205 GPa for bars) up to fpd​=fp0,1k​/γs​, then either an inclined branch towards (εuk​,fpk​/γs​) bounded at εud​, or a horizontal plateau without limit:

σp​=fpd​+(γs​fpk​​−fpd​)εuk​−fpd​/Ep​εp​−fpd​/Ep​​(εp​≤εud​)(21.7)

The default law is that of the Y1860S7 strand: fp0,1k​=1640 MPa, fpk​=1860 MPa, εuk​=3.5 %, εud​=0.9εuk​. A tendon enters the section through its position, its area and its initial elongation Δεp​(0) (§ 6.1(6), figure 6.1): its strain when the concrete at its level is unstrained. keta computes this elongation from the stress σpm​ of the tendon and the stress σcp​ of the concrete at its level, by inverting the law on its rising branch:

Δεp​(0)=σp−1​(σpm​)−Ecm​σcp​​(21.8)

A bonded tendon then carries σp​(Δεp​(0)+ε(yp​,zp​)). An unbonded tendon keeps the stress of its initial elongation; at the ultimate limit state, this stress is increased by a fixed Δσp,ULS​ (100 MPa recommended, § 5.10.8(2)), without exceeding the top of the law.

21.3 Equilibrium of a section#

21.3.1 Strain plane and stress resultants#

Everything that follows rests on the same computation: the resultants of a strain plane. With ε(y,z)=ε0​+κy​z−κz​y, the forces are, at the origin of the axes of the section,

​NMy​Mz​​​=∫Ac​​σc​(ε)​1z−y​​dA+i∑​Ai​σi​(ε0,i​+ε(yi​,zi​))​1zi​−yi​​​(21.9)

where the sum is over the bars and the bonded tendons, each with its initial strain ε0,i​ (zero for a bar cast in an unloaded section; negative for a bar that has restrained creep and shrinkage). A positive My​ puts the top fibre in tension (chapter 2). The tangent stiffness ∂(N,My​,Mz​)/∂(ε0​,κy​,κz​) is obtained by the same integrals with the tangent modulus of the laws.

21.3.2 Boundary integrals#

Under a plane, the stress in the concrete depends only on the coordinate s taken along the strain gradient. With t the transverse coordinate, Green's theorem reduces each surface integral to an integral over the outlines, traversed anticlockwise (the voids clockwise):

∫Ac​​f(s)tkdA=−∮f(s)k+1tk+1​ds(21.10)

less the same integral around each disc of concrete displaced by a steel. Along an edge, the strain is linear; the edge is cut at the kinks of the law (zero strain, start of the plateau, yield limits of a steel), and each piece is integrated by a 16-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature after the change of variable ξ↦ξ2(3−2ξ), whose derivative vanishes at both ends. The result is exact for polynomial laws (parabola of exponent 2, bilinear relation, straight line), exact to within rounding for a fractional exponent or for the Sargin law, and the change of variable absorbs the fractional power of a parabola at the start of its plateau. There is neither a mesh nor a subdivision of the compression zone. On a 0.30 × 0.60 m rectangle reinforced with 3 HA 20 at 5 cm from the edge, in C30/37 at fcd​=17 MPa, at pivot B with a steel having an inclined branch, keta finds a resisting moment of 213.972 kN·m, the value of the closed form of the parabola-rectangle diagram (α=17/21, ka​=99/238) to within 10−15.

The fibre section engine, used for moment-curvature curves and nonlinear bars (chapter 18), instead divides a rectangle into fibres of area Aj​, to which the bars and tendons are added, and replaces the integral by the sum ∑j​σ(εj​)Aj​.

21.3.3 Search for the equilibrium state#

For a given action effect S=(N,My​,Mz​), the state of the section is the plane e=(ε0​,κy​,κz​) that solves R(e)=S. keta seeks it by the damped Newton method:

(Kt​(ek​)+μK0​)Δe=S−R(ek​),ek+1​=ek​+2−jΔe(21.11)

The starting point is the plane of the section on its initial moduli: with concrete without tension, the tangent at the zero plane is that of the steels alone, and the first step would be wrong. The step is halved (at most 40 times) as long as the norm of the residual does not decrease. When the tangent allows no progress (nothing in compression and nothing bonded responds to the residual), it is supplemented by a share μ of the initial stiffness, multiplied by 10 at each failure and reduced after each success; beyond μ=103, the action effect is declared beyond the reach of the section. The moments are compared with the forces through the size of the section. The computation stops when the relative residual falls below 10−13, or below 10−10 if it can no longer decrease, in at most 200 iterations. A state in which a vertex of the concrete, a bonded tendon or a bar exceeds the limit strain of its law is refused: it is a resistance, not a state. The cracked state derives from a convex potential and its plane is unique; with a softening law (Sargin beyond εc1​, tension softening), the plane found is an equilibrium whose uniqueness is not proven.

The fibre engine uses the same method, with the full 3×3 tangent matrix, a gradient descent on the maximum secant stiffness when the tangent is singular (plastic plateau), a line search that stays within the strain limits of the laws, a tolerance of 10−8 relative to each component of the target, and at most 100 iterations.

21.3.4 Composite section without a mesh#

A section made of several materials (steel girder under a slab, concrete cast in two strengths, encased section) is described by its parts, each with its outlines and its law: concrete (parabola-rectangle, Sargin, tension softening), straight line, bilinear steel with a plateau or with hardening. All share the strain plane, as do the bonded point reinforcements:

R(e)=parts p∑​∫Ap​​σp​(ε)(1,z,−y)dA+i∑​Ai​σi​(ε0,i​+εi​)(1,zi​,−yi​)(21.12)

Each integral is the boundary integral (21.10) of the law of its part; a part lodged within another is drawn as a void of the latter. The state under an action effect comes from the same damped iteration, and keta gives what each part carries and the stress in each steel. The resisting moment of a composite section is not computed by this engine.

21.4 Stresses at serviceability#

21.4.1 Rectangular or T section#

For a rectangular section, or a T section with its flange in compression, reinforced with two layers (tension As​ at the effective depth d, compression As2​ at d2​), in uniaxial bending with an axial force applied at the gross centroid, keta gives the two states of EN 1992-1-1 § 7.1(2). The modular ratio accounts for creep through the effective modulus (expression 7.20):

αe​=Ec,eff​Es​​=Ecm​Es​(1+φ)​(21.13)

In the uncracked state, the whole section participates, the steels being counted with αe​−1 (the steel replaces the concrete). In the cracked state, the concrete in tension is neglected, the tension steels are counted with αe​ and the compression steels with αe​−1. The neutral axis x is the depth at which the resultant of the linear stress block passes through the point of application of the action; in simple bending, it is the root of the equation of first moments:

2bx2​+(αe​−1)As2​(x−d2​)=αe​As​(d−x),σc​=−III​Mx​,σs​=αe​III​M(d−x)​(21.14)

keta finds it by bisection on an interval, scanned between 0 and 4h, where the function changes sign; a section that cannot balance the action in the cracked state (tension over the whole depth) is refused. For the 0.30 × 0.60 m rectangle reinforced with 3 HA 20 (d=0.55 m) under 150 kN·m, without creep (φ=0, Ecm​=32.84 GPa, αe​=6.09), keta finds x=0.1272 m, σs​=313.5 MPa and σc​=−15.49 MPa, the values of the hand solution of (21.14). The cracking moment is the moment that brings the bottom fibre of the uncracked state to fct,eff​ (by default fctm​ of table 3.1, 0.30fck2/3​ up to C50/60 and 2.12ln(1+fcm​/10) beyond).

21.4.2 Uncracked and prestressed polygonal section#

For an arbitrary polygonal section, as long as the concrete is uncracked, the state is linear: concrete of the outlines with modulus Ecm​, tendons with modulus Ep​, bars with modulus Es​. A bonded tendon follows the concrete at its level from its initial elongation, an unbonded tendon keeps its force, a bar follows the concrete from a stress-free state:

σp,i​=Ep​Δεp,i​(0)+Ecm​Ep​​σc​(yi​,zi​)  (bonded),σp,i​=Ep​Δεp,i​(0)  (unbonded),σs,j​=Es​ε0,j​+Ecm​Es​​σc​(yj​,zj​)(21.15)

The concrete carries the action effect less the forces in the steels, and its stress is a plane:

σc​(y,z)=Ac​Nc​​+bending due to (My,c​,Mz,c​),(Nc​,My,c​,Mz,c​)=(N,My​,Mz​)−i∑​Ai​σi​(1, zi​, −yi​)(21.16)

These relations form a linear system. With bonded tendons, its solution is N/A+Mz/I of the transformed section Ac​+(Ep​/Ecm​)Ap​ under the action effect and the decompression forces Ap​Ep​Δεp​(0) applied in compression at the tendons. The concrete is that of the outlines less the concrete displaced by the steels: one disc per tendon (the area of the duct while it is empty, the area of the tendon once grouted or for a pretensioned wire), centred if necessary beside the tendon, which bears on the wall of its duct, and counted for its area, its first moments and its own second moment of area a2/(4π); on request, one disc per bar. A disc that extends outside the concrete or overlaps another is refused. A plane reaches its extremes over polygons at vertices: the extreme fibres are the vertex in greatest tension and the vertex in greatest compression of the outlines. keta gives the stress in each tendon and each bar, that of the concrete at their level and at any requested point (a point outside the concrete is refused), the extreme fibres and the strain plane.

21.4.3 Cracked state and nonlinear state#

When the concrete no longer follows a straight line, the state is the plane that balances the action effect in the sense of (21.9). In the cracked state, the concrete is elastic in compression and carries nothing in tension, the steels remaining elastic:

σc​(ε)=Ec​min(ε,0),σs​=Es​(ε0,s​+ε),Ec​=Ecm​ or 1+φEcm​​(21.17)

the effective modulus being given for a long-term action. In the nonlinear state, each material follows its law: the concrete the parabola-rectangle, the Sargin law, the parabola-rectangle with tension softening or a straight line; bonded tendons the law of prestressing steel from Δεp​(0); bars the bilinear curve of figure 3.8. The force of a tendon at decompression acts as an external compression at the tendon: for a rectangular or T section, the equilibrium equation reduces to the classical cubic equation of the neutral axis. A section that the action leaves in compression everywhere is in its uncracked state. On the previous rectangle, the cracked state of the polygonal section reproduces the neutral axis and the steel stress of the closed form.

21.4.4 Choice of state#

EN 1992-1-1 § 7.1(2) allows the stresses to be computed on the uncracked section as long as the flexural tensile stress does not exceed fct,eff​. keta computes the uncracked state, reads its largest concrete stress and switches to the cracked state beyond:

verticesmax​σcI​≤fct,eff​ ⇒ uncracked state;otherwise cracked state(21.18)

The choice is based on the given action effect alone. A section cracked by an earlier, larger action effect remains cracked: keta does not know this, and it is then up to the user to request the cracked state directly.

21.5 Moment-curvature and deflections#

21.5.1 Moment-curvature curve#

For a fibre section (rectangle, bars, bonded or unbonded tendons), keta plots the curve M(κ) at constant axial force: for each curvature, the strain at the centre ε0​ is sought by bisection on the equation N(ε0​,κ)=NEd​, and the moment is read. The curve stops at the ultimate point, the largest curvature whose axial equilibrium keeps all the fibres and all the bonded tendons within the limits of their law:

κu​=max{κ : ∃ε0​, N(ε0​,κ)=NEd​, εmin,j​≤ε0,j​+ε0​+κzj​≤εmax,j​ ∀j}(21.19)

A limit strain may be imposed on steels with a plateau, which have none of their own. The curve is plotted in bending about y; the ultimate point may be sought in any direction of bending.

21.5.2 Mean curvature and deflection#

For the rectangular or T section, the mean curvature of a cracked member interpolates the curvatures of the two states according to EN 1992-1-1 § 7.4.3, expressions (7.18) and (7.19):

κ=ζκII​+(1−ζ)κI​,ζ=1−β(σs​σsr​​)2=1−β(MMcr​​)2(21.20)

with β=1 for a single short-term loading and 0.5 for sustained or repeated loading; ζ=0 below the cracking moment. The mid-span deflection of a simply supported beam under a given moment diagram is the unit-load integral δ=∫0L​κ(x)mˉ(x)dx, mˉ=x/2 or (L−x)/2, computed by Simpson's rule on each half-span. Shrinkage adds the curvature of expression (7.21),

rcs​1​=εcs​αe​IS​(21.21)

where S is the first moment of the reinforcement about the centroid of the transformed section (state I) or about the neutral axis (state II) and I the corresponding second moment of area. The deflection with shrinkage interpolates the total curvature with the same ζ; it is integrated by an adaptive 5-point Gauss-Legendre quadrature to 10−12 in relative terms, on the pieces lying between the cracking points ∣M∣=Mcr​, located over 256 intervals and then refined by bisection.

21.6 Ultimate resistance to combined bending and axial force#

21.6.1 Ultimate strain planes: pivots A, B and C#

At the ultimate limit state (EN 1992-1-1 § 6.1(5), figure 6.1), the strain plane of a section at failure passes through one of three pivots. For a direction α of the neutral axis, keta measures s along u=(cosα,sinα), compression being on the side of u, and writes the plane ε(s)=εtop​+g(s−smax​), h=smax​−smin​ being the depth of concrete in this direction. A parameter τ∈[0,3] runs through the planes from the most tensioned to the most compressed:

​A (0≤τ≤1):B (1≤τ≤2):C (2≤τ≤3):​εtop​εtop​εtop​​=εa​−τ(εa​+εcu​),=−εcu​,=−εcu​+(τ−2)(εcu​−εc​),​gε(smin​)ε(smax​−(1−εcu​εc​​)h)​=imax​smax​−si​εtop​−εlim,i​​=(2−τ)εbotA​=−εc​​(21.22)

At pivot A, the first steel to reach its limit εlim,i​ sets the slope: a bar at εud​−ε0,i​, a bonded tendon limited to εud​−Δεp​(0); εa​ is the smallest of these limits, and τ=0 is the uniform tension εa​. Without steel, the furthest concrete fibre serves as the pivot. At pivot B, the most compressed fibre is at crushing −εcu​ and the opposite fibre goes from its value at the end of pivot A to zero. At pivot C, the plane rotates about the point located at (1−εc​/εcu​)h from the most compressed fibre, up to the uniform compression −εc​. For the parabola-rectangle, εcu​=εcu2​ and εc​=εc2​; for another law, they are its compressive limit strain and the strain at which it reaches its largest compression (εcu1​ and εc1​ for the Sargin law). A law that carries tension is refused: its tensile limit would be one more pivot. The axial force decreases as τ increases.

21.6.2 Resisting moment in a given direction#

The resisting moment at the axial force NEd​, in the direction θ of (My​,Mz​), is sought in two loops. For a direction α of the neutral axis, the axial force decreases with τ: bisection gives the plane that carries NEd​, to within 10−15 on τ; if NEd​ lies outside the interval [N(τ=3),N(τ=0)], it is beyond the axial capacity. Then α is swept over 144 values around the circle; the component of the resisting moment perpendicular to the requested direction changes sign where that moment is parallel to it (and in the same sense), and a second bisection refines α. A sample at which this component is already zero, to within 10−12 of the moment, is retained as it is: this is the case of a doubly symmetric section loaded along a principal axis (θ=0 or π/2), where the component vanishes without changing sign. On the 0.40 × 0.60 m rectangle reinforced with 6 HA 20 of figure 21.5, under N=−1 MN, keta thus finds 431.1 kN·m for θ=0 and 247.9 kN·m for θ=π/2. The direction is defined by

MR​(α)×dθ​=0,MR​⋅dθ​>0,dθ​=(cosθ,sinθ),MRd​=∣MR​∣(21.23)

The concrete is integrated by the boundary integrals of its law, by default the parabola-rectangle of table 3.1 for fck​ at fcd​; the bars follow (21.6) from their initial strain. The steels are points: by default, the concrete they displace is not deducted, as in design charts; on request, the disc of each tendon and each bar is removed.

21.6.3 Interaction diagrams#

The N-M interaction diagram of a direction α is the sequence of the resultants of the ultimate planes for τ distributed over [0,3] (61 points by default), in a single pass and without root finding. The My​-Mz​ diagram at constant axial force is obtained by rotating θ; keta also gives, for a fibre section, the curve of the ultimate points of several bending directions at constant N, the steel with a plateau then being limited (1 % by default).

The ends of the diagram can be checked by hand. In uniform tension εud​, the six bars carry 6As​ftd​=0.860 MN. In uniform compression −εc2​=−2 ‰, the concrete carries bhfcd​=4.080 MN and the bars, still elastic since 2 ‰<εyd​=2.17 ‰, 6As​Es​εc2​=0.754 MN: keta finds 4.834 MN, and not bhfcd​+As​fyd​=4.900 MN. The capacity is sought at fixed axial force, in the direction of the moment; the capacity along a ray of the space (N,My​,Mz​), at constant eccentricity, is not computed.

21.6.4 Prestressed sections#

In the resistance engine, a bonded tendon follows the plane from its initial elongation, σp​(Δεp​(0)+ε), and its limit enters pivot A; an unbonded tendon carries min(σp​(Δεp​(0))+Δσp,ULS​, σp,max​) whatever the plane. A section without bars or without tendons is accepted. To connect the section to a structural analysis, keta gives the primary action of the prestress, opposite to the resultant of the tendon forces at their initial elongation,

(N,My​,Mz​)iso​=i∑​(−Pi​, −Pi​zi​, Pi​yi​),Pi​=Ap,i​σp​(Δεp,i​(0))(21.24)

and splits a total effect of the prestress, read on the framework, into this primary part and a secondary (hyperstatic) part, the difference of the two. The tendons are assumed normal to the section: their inclination is not taken into account in the section.

21.6.5 Rectangular section with the rectangular stress block#

For the rectangular or T section, keta also computes the resisting moment with the rectangular stress block (21.3), the top fibre at εcu3​ and the steels elastic-perfectly plastic (without strain limit): the neutral axis x is the root, found by bisection, of the force equilibrium, and the moment is taken at the gross centroid,

−ηfcd​Ac​(λx)+As​σs​+As2​σs2​=N,MRd​=Fc​zc​+As​σs​d+As2​σs2​d2​−NzG​(21.25)

with fcd​=αcc​fck​/γc​. For the 0.30 × 0.60 m rectangle with 3 HA 20 and αcc​=1, keta finds x=85.4 mm and MRd​=211.38 kN·m, the value of As​fyd​(d−λx/2).

21.7 Shear, torsion and punching shear#

These checks are the formulae of EN 1992-1-1, given one by one with their clause, and those of the German national annex where it modifies them; they return values, which the user combines.

21.7.1 Shear#

The resistance without shear reinforcement is expression (6.2):

VRd,c​=max(CRd,c​k(100ρl​fck​)1/3+k1​σcp​, vmin​+k1​σcp​)bw​d,k=1+200/d​≤2(21.26)

with ρl​≤0.02, σcp​=NEd​/Ac​<0.2fcd​, and, in the EN, CRd,c​=0.18/γc​, k1​=0.15, vmin​=0.035k3/2fck1/2​ (6.3N); in the German annex CRd,c​=0.15/γc​, k1​=0.12 and vmin​=(0.0525/γc​)k3/2fck1/2​ for d≤600 mm. For a slab with d=0.25 m, ρl​=0.8 % and C30/37, keta gives 163.93 kN/m. With vertical reinforcement (§ 6.2.3), the lever arm is z=0.9d (limited in the German annex by max(d−cv,l​−30 mm, d−2cv,l​)), and

sAsw​​=zfywd​cotθVEd​​(6.8),VRd,max​=cotθ+tanθαcw​bw​zν1​fcd​​(6.9),ν=0.6(1−250fck​​)(21.27)

The German annex gives ν1​=0.75min(1; 1.1−fck​/500), the concrete contribution VRd,cc​=0.5⋅0.48fck1/3​(1−1.2σcd​/fcd​)bw​z and the inclination cotθ=(1.2+1.4σcd​/fcd​)/(1−VRd,cc​/VEd​) limited to [1;3] (1.75 for bridges). The minimum ratio is ρw,min​=0.08fck​​/fyk​ (9.5N). The shear force is not reduced for ΔFtd​ (6.18), and the resistance of regions uncracked in bending, governed by the principal tensile stress (6.4), is not computed.

21.7.2 Torsion, web-flange shear and construction joints#

Torsion follows the equivalent box of § 6.3.2: for a given thickness tef​ (in the German annex, twice the distance from the face to the axis of the longitudinal reinforcement), Ak​=(b−tef​)(h−tef​) and uk​=2(b+h−2tef​), and

τt​tef​=2Ak​TEd​​ (6.26),sAsw​​=2Ak​fyd​TEd​tanθ​,Asl​=2Ak​fyd​TEd​uk​cotθ​ (6.28),TRd,max​=2ναcw​fcd​Ak​tef​sinθcosθ (6.30)(21.28)

The transverse reinforcement of a flange follows expression (6.21), Asf​/sf​=vEd​hf​/(cotθf​fyd​). The shear along a construction joint follows expression (6.25), vRdi​=cfctd​+μσn​+ρfyd​(μsinα+cosα) (1.2μ in the steel term for the German annex), from which keta derives the required reinforcement ratio and the limit 0.5νfcd​.

21.7.3 Punching shear#

For a rectangular internal column a×b, the basic control perimeter at 2d is u1​=2(a+b)+4πd (§ 6.4.2), the design shear stress vEd​=βVEd​/(u1​d) (6.38) and the resistance

vRd,c​=CRd,c​k(100ρl​fck​)1/3+0.1σcp​≥vmin​+0.1σcp​,ρl​=ρly​ρlz​​≤0.02(6.47)(21.29)

The German annex reduces CRd,c​ to 0.18/γc​(0.1u0​/d+0.6) when u0​/d<4, limits ρl​ by 0.5fcd​/fyd​, sets β according to the position of the column (1.10 internal, 1.40 edge, 1.50 corner, 1.35 and 1.20 at the end and at the corner of a wall) and vRd,max​=1.4vRd,c​. The method of the Swiss standard SIA 262 (§ 4.3.6) is also available: τcd​=0.3ηt​fck​​/γc​, slab rotation at level of approximation III ψ=1.2(rs​/d)(fsd​/Es​)(msd​/mRd​)1.5, kr​=1/(0.45+0.18ψdkg​) and VRd,c​=kr​τcd​dured​.

21.8 Serviceability limit states#

21.8.1 Stress limits#

Clause 7.2 of EN 1992-1-1 names five stress limits:

σc​≤k1​fck​,σc​≤k2​fck​,σs​≤k3​fyk​,σs​≤k4​fyk​,σp​≤k5​fpk​(21.30)

the compression of the concrete under the characteristic combination in exposure classes XD, XF and XS, the compression under quasi-permanent loads below which creep is linear, the tension of the reinforcement under the characteristic combination and under an imposed deformation, and the mean stress of the tendons. The recommended values are 0.6, 0.45, 0.8, 1 and 0.75; a national annex may give others. The tendon limit refers to fpk​, as in the 2004 text and its French version; the consolidated British reprints give fyk​, a misprint that no corrigendum has corrected. For a serviceability state (uncracked, cracked or nonlinear), keta gives the ratio of each stress to its limit: the compression at the most compressed vertex, the largest tension in the bars and that in the tendons. It is up to the user to know which combination each ratio belongs to.

21.8.2 Crack width#

Crack width follows § 7.3.4 of EN 1992-1-1, the 2010 corrigendum included:

wk​=sr,max​(εsm​−εcm​),εsm​−εcm​=Es​σs​−kt​ρp,eff​fct,eff​​(1+αe​ρp,eff​)​ ≥ 0.6Es​σs​​(21.31)
sr,max​=k3​c+k1​k2​k4​ρp,eff​ϕ​,ρp,eff​=Ac,eff​As​+ξ1​Ap′​​,ξ1​=ξϕp​ϕs​​​(21.32)

(ξ​ with tendons alone), and sr,max​=1.3(h−x) (7.14) when the bars are spaced more than 5(c+ϕ/2) apart or when no bonded steel lies within the effective area. The default coefficients are k1​=0.8 (high bond), k2​=0.5 (bending), k3​=3.4, k4​=0.425 and kt​=0.6 (short term). On a polygonal section, the geometric quantities are read along the strain gradient of the cracked state: h is the depth of the section in this direction, x the compression depth, d the depth of the centroid of the tension bars (of the bonded tendons in tension if there is no bar). The effective area is the concrete lying within

hc,ef​=min(2.5(h−d), (h−x)/3)(21.33)

of the fibre in greatest tension, obtained by cutting each outline with a straight line: it is exact for a polygon with voids and an oblique neutral axis. The h/2 term of the standard is never governing when a zone is in compression, since (h−x)/3<h/3. The bars and bonded tendons whose centre lies within this band enter ρp,eff​; σs​ is the change in stress of the bar in greatest tension from the zero strain of the concrete at its level, Es​ times the strain of the plane, or failing a bar that of the bonded tendon in greatest tension. Expression (7.10) carries ξ1​ since the 2010 corrigendum; the earlier text carried ξ12​, a form that the German version keeps and that keta offers as an option. A section without a compression zone (tie, figure 7.1 c) is refused by this computation: the chain (7.8) to (7.14) remains available on its own, the user giving the effective area.

For the 0.30 × 0.60 m rectangle with 3 HA 20 under 150 kN·m, the cover and diameter of expression (7.11) being left at their default values (30 mm and 16 mm, not those of the bars of the section), keta finds hc,ef​=125 mm, ρp,eff​=2.51 %, sr,max​=210 mm and wk​=0.246 mm, by hand as on the polygonal section. The variant of the German annex computes sr,max​=ϕ/(3.6ρeff​)≤σs​ϕ/(3.6fct,eff​) without prestress.

21.8.3 Simplified control and minimum reinforcement#

The minimum area of crack-control reinforcement follows expressions (7.1) and (7.2) for rectangles and webs:

As,min​σs​=kc​kfct,eff​Act​,kc​=0.4[1−k1​(h/h∗)fct,eff​σc​​]∈[0,1](21.34)

with h∗=min(h,1 m), k1​=1.5 in compression and 2h∗/(3h) in tension. The coefficient k for self-equilibrating stresses is that of the German annex, 0.8 for h≤300 mm and 0.5 for h≥800 mm, linear in between; the EN value (1.0 to 0.65) and the kc​ of T sections and boxes are not coded. Control without direct calculation follows table 7.2DE of the German annex, written as a formula, σs​=3.48⋅106wk​/ϕs∗​​ (MPa, wk​ and ϕs∗​ in mm), with the diameter conversion ϕs​=ϕs∗​fct,eff​/2.9 MPa for minimum reinforcement; tables 7.2N and 7.3N of the EN are not coded.

21.8.4 Brittle failure#

The uncracked state is linear: under the sustained action effect increased by a moment M of direction θ, the stress at a vertex j is σj​=σcp,j​+M/Wj​(θ), where σcp,j​ is its stress under the prestress and the sustained action effect and Wj​ the section modulus of the transformed section at that point. The cracking moment is the smallest moment that brings a vertex to fct​:

Mcr​=jmin​(fct​−σcp,j​)Wj​(θ)(21.35)

The prestress therefore shifts the cracking moment by −σcp​W. Computed on the section with the tendons released (zero initial elongations), it is the moment Mrep​ of EN 1992-2 § 6.1(109) b), from which the minimum reinforcement that prevents brittle failure is derived:

As,min​=zs​fyk​Mrep​​(6.101a),As,min​fyk​+Ap​Δσp​≥zMrep​​(6.101b),Δσp​=min(0.4fptk​; 500 MPa)(21.36)

zs​ is the lever arm of the reinforcing bars at the ultimate limit state, read on the ultimate plane that balances the axial force: the distance between the point of application of the resultant of the compressed concrete and that of the resultant of the tension bars. On the 0.30 × 0.60 m rectangle with no reinforcement counted, Mcr​=fctm​bh2/6=52.14 kN·m. Method a) of § 6.1(109), by reduction of the prestressing area, is not coded.

21.8.5 Fatigue#

keta gives the quantities of the simplified method of § 6.8: the design fatigue strength of concrete (6.76), the reference stress range of straight and bent bars at N∗=106 cycles (table 6.3N: 162.5 MPa; 175 MPa in the German annex), and the damage-equivalent stress range:

fcd,fat​=k1​βcc​(t0​)fcd​(1−250fck​​),Δσs,equ​(N∗)=λs​(σs,max​−σs,min​)(21.37)

with k1​=0.85 (EN) or 1.0 (German annex). The stresses come from the serviceability states described above; the damage computation of the structure under traffic is in chapter 14.

21.9 Prestress losses at section level#

The losses are computed on the transformed serviceability section: concrete of the outlines less the voids and the displaced concrete, modulus Ecm​; bonded tendons at their initial elongation, unbonded tendons at a frozen force. The elastic shortening of a tendon under the prestress alone is (Ep​/Ecm​)∣σc​∣, σc​ being the stress of the concrete at its level (§ 5.10.5.1): this is the whole loss of a pretensioned wire, and for n post-tensioned tendons stressed one after another, the mean share j=(n−1)/(2n) (expression 5.44). Between t0​ and t, each steel follows the concrete at its level, which shortens by shrinkage, by creep under the quasi-permanent stress present at t0​, and by the deformation, on the adjusted modulus Ecm​/(1+χφ), due to the change of stress that the losses themselves cause. Written for each steel i (tendon or bar) of modulus Ei​, compatibility gives the linear system

Δσi​+Ecm​Ei​​(1+χφ)j∑​fij​Aj​Δσj​=−εcs​Ei​+ρΔσpr,i​−Ecm​Ei​​φσc,QP,i​,fij​=Ac​1​+ei​⋅Ic−1​⋅ej​(21.38)

where Δσi​ is the tension lost (positive), fij​ the stress of the concrete at the level of steel i per unit force at steel j (eccentricities e in biaxial bending), χ the ageing coefficient and ρ the retained share of the pure relaxation, both 0.8 in EN 1992-1-1 and adjustable; relaxation is zero for a bar, εcs​<0 is a shortening and σc​<0 a compression. With a single tendon and no bar, this is expression (5.46); on a 0.50 × 1.00 m rectangle with a tendon of 1500 mm² at an eccentricity of 0.35 m, at φ=2, εcs​=−300⋅10−6 and 40 MPa of pure relaxation, keta finds 169.60 MPa, the value of (5.46). With several tendons, the same compatibility couples them: tendons at the same point lose as a single tendon of their total area, and the loss of one tendon relieves the concrete at the others. Bars restrain creep and shrinkage: they go into compression, unload the concrete, and the loss of the tendons is reduced. keta gives the loss of each steel by cause (creep, shrinkage, relaxation) and the plane of the change of stress in the concrete.

After the losses, each steel keeps the initial strain

ε0,i​=Ei​σi​−Δσi​​−Ecm​σc,iafter​​(21.39)

its strain when the concrete at its level, at the stress that the losses have left there, is unloaded. Carried into the section, for tendons as for bars, it makes the uncracked state under the same action effect the state after losses, from which subsequent actions start: imposed load, cracking, resisting moment. A sequence of ages can be computed with the laws of EN 1992-1-1: creep and shrinkage of annex B, shrinkage counted from tensioning, relaxation of expressions (3.28) to (3.30) at time t−t0​, without the 500 000 h cap of § 3.3.2(8). Each value is the cumulative loss since t0​ on the section as it is at t0​.

21.10 Design of reinforcement#

21.10.1 Arbitrary section#

For a polygonal section under (NEd​,My,Ed​,Mz,Ed​), the user lays out the bars and gives them relative weights wi​; keta seeks the smallest factor ω such that the section with areas Ai​=ωwi​ carries the action effect:

ω∗=min{ω∈[0,ωmax​] : MRd​(ω; NEd​,θEd​)≥∣MEd​∣},θEd​=atan2(Mz,Ed​,My,Ed​)(21.40)

by bisection to within 10−15ωmax​, assuming that the resistance increases with ω. The total area is ω∗∑wi​. The distribution between the bars is therefore the one the user sets: there is neither optimisation by independent zones, nor several simultaneous action effects, nor prestress in this design, nor automatic choice of the diameters.

21.10.2 Rectangular section#

For a rectangle in combined bending and axial force, keta computes the steel areas in closed form from the reduced moment, with the parabola-rectangle diagram and the steel of figure 3.8:

μ=bd2fcd​MEds​​,μ=αR​ξ(1−ka​ξ),As1​=σs1​1​(ζdMEds​​+NEd​)(21.41)

where MEds​ is the moment referred to the tension steel, αR​ and ka​ the exact coefficients of the parabola-rectangle block for the concrete strain, and ζ=1−ka​ξ. The plane is at pivot A (steel at its limit, concrete strain sought by bisection) or at pivot B (εcu2​, ξ the root of a quadratic equation). Beyond ξlim​ (0.45 up to C50/60 for a linear elastic analysis, German annex 5.4), the compression zone is frozen and the remainder ΔM=MEds​−Mlim​ is carried by a couple of steels: As1​=(Mlim​/(ζd)+ΔM/(d−d2​)+NEd​)/σs1​ and As2​=ΔM/((d−d2​)∣σs2​∣).

21.11 Slabs and shells#

21.11.1 Wood-Armer moments#

A slab reinforced with two layers, along x and along a direction y′ at the angle α to x, must resist the moment tensor S=[mx​mxy​​mxy​my​​] on every yield line. A layer of capacity X per unit width resists, on a line of normal n, X(e1​⋅n)2 (Johansen's criterion); the condition is that Xe1​e1T​+YaaT−S be positive semi-definite, a=(cosα,sinα). It reduces to the orthogonal case on Armer's transformed tensor:

s11′​=mx​−2mxy​cotα+my​cot2α,s12′​=sinαmxy​−my​cotα​,s22′​=sin2αmy​​(21.42)

and the minimum of X+Y is in closed form (Wood's rules, 1968):

X=s11′​+∣s12′​∣,Y=s22′​+∣s12′​∣;if X<0: X=0, Y=s22′​+∣s11′​∣s12′2​​(and symmetrically)(21.43)

and no steel is required when both remain negative. The top steel resists S, the bottom steel −S (a positive moment puts the +z face of the facet in tension, chapter 24); the design moments are returned signed, positive on the top face and negative on the bottom face. Since the method is not linear, the moments must be combined before design; the envelope over several combinations then takes the maximum of the top values and the minimum of the bottom values. For (mx​,my​,mxy​)=(10,−8,3) kN·m/m, keta gives mx,top​=10+9/8=11.125 and my,bot​=−(8+9/10)=−8.9.

21.11.2 Assessment of given capacities#

Given the capacities of the four layers, the utilisation of a face is the smallest λ≥0 such that λC−S is positive semi-definite, C=Xe1​e1T​+YaaT: it is the largest ratio of action effect to capacity over all yield-line directions (Denton and Burgoyne, 1996). The search over the angle is done exactly: the admissible set of λ is a half-line whose origin is 0 or a root of one of the three polynomial conditions for a positive semi-definite 2×2 matrix,

λC11​−S11​≥0,λC22​−S22​≥0,(λC11​−S11​)(λC22​−S22​)−(λC12​−S12​)2≥0(21.44)

and these candidates are tried in increasing order. The utilisation is infinite when a direction in tension has no capacity; keta also returns the normal of the critical line.

21.11.3 Sandwich model for shells#

For a shell element subjected to the six stress resultants, the forces are carried by two layers at the levels of the steels ztop​>0 and zbot​<0 from the mid-surface:

ntop​=ztop​−zbot​m−nzbot​​,nbot​=ztop​−zbot​nztop​−m​(21.45)

component by component, each layer being designed by the same kernel on its membrane tensor (Clark-Nielsen method); keta gives the steel forces and the remaining principal concrete force. A second formulation, that of Baumann (EN 1992-1-1 annex F) with the strut at 45°, distributes n/2±m/z between the layers (z=0.9d by default), gives the orthogonal steels of each layer, Zx​=Nx​+∣Nxy​∣ and Zy​=Ny​+∣Nxy​∣, or Zx​=0 and Zy​=Ny​+Nxy2​/∣Nx​∣ when Nx​<−∣Nxy​∣, and treats the transverse shear force v0​=qx2​+qy2​​ by (21.26) then (21.27).

21.12 Composite beams and steel members#

21.12.1 Steel-concrete composite beams#

For composite beams, keta gives the formulae of EN 1994-1-1 with their intermediate quantities: resistance of headed studs (§ 6.6.3.1) and reduction for profiled sheeting with transverse ribs (§ 6.6.4.2), effective width (§ 5.4.1.2), plastic resisting moment in sagging, plastic neutral axis in the slab, the flange or the web, and partial shear connection by the linear interpolation (6.1), plastic resisting moment in hogging with the class of the compressed plates, uncracked and cracked elastic section, long-term modular ratios (5.6), deflection of a simply supported span with its construction stage, minimum degree of shear connection (6.12 to 6.17), cracked lengths for global analysis (15 % of the span), stiffness of the inverted U-frame and table 6.1 for lateral-torsional buckling, composite columns (§ 6.7: Npl,Rd​, plastic N-M interaction, effective flexural stiffness, simplified method) and beams with large web openings according to the SCI P355 guide (Lawson and Hicks, 2011). For example:

PRd​=γv​min(0.8fu​πd2/4, 0.29αd2fck​Ecm​​)​,MRd​=Mpl,a,Rd​+(Mpl,Rd​−Mpl,a,Rd​)η,nL​=n0​(1+ψL​φt​)(21.46)

The steel section enters through its actual dimensions and its tabulated A and Wpl​, fillets included.

21.12.2 Steel members#

Likewise, keta gives the check formulae of EN 1993-1-1 and EN 1993-1-5: class of the plates (table 5.2), buckling factors kσ​ and reduction of slender plates,

λˉp​=28.4εkσ​​b/t​,ρ=λˉp2​λˉp​−0.055(3+ψ)​≤1,χ=Φ+Φ2−λˉ2​1​,Φ=21​[1+α(λˉ−0.2)+λˉ2](21.47)

effective section under uniform compression, stiffeners on an elastic foundation (annex A.2), cross-section resistances (shear, interaction with moment and axial force), flexural and lateral-torsional buckling curves (tables 6.1 to 6.5), interaction factors of annexes A and B. For λˉ=1 on curve b, keta finds χ=0.5970. The quantities that the standard leaves to “an appropriate method” (Mcr​, Ncr,T​, deflections) come from the structural analyses, in particular from non-uniform torsion (chapter 19).

21.13 Scope#

  • the serviceability states and the resistance apply to polygonal sections with voids and point steels; the rectangular or T section in closed form is limited to uniaxial bending and two layers, the flange being assumed in compression;
  • the resistance engine accepts for the concrete only the parabola-rectangle (free exponent and strains) and the Sargin law; laws carrying tension, the piecewise cubic law and structural steel as an outline material do not enter it; the composite section without a mesh has no resisting moment;
  • confined concrete, aged strength and modulus in the section laws, and the stretching of the ultimate law by creep are not treated;
  • the capacity is computed at fixed axial force in the direction of the moment, not along a ray of the space (N,My​,Mz​);
  • the tendons are normal to the section; their inclination enters only the structural analysis (chapter 8);
  • the choice of the cracked state is based on the present action effect alone; the cracking history is the user's responsibility;
  • the principal tensile stress in the webs, the classification of the fibres inside and outside the cover zone and the strain at the centroid on the ultimate plane are not provided;
  • the design keeps the distribution of the bars given by the user; it chooses neither diameters, nor layers, nor spacings.
